title: Dolores Huerta's death sparks an outpouring from allies and admirers
text:
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (AP) — Dolores Huerta’s death on Wednesday provoked an outpouring of emotions from many who had worked with her on social causes and resonated far and wide among others inspired by her legacy. They shared stories about becoming public servants, volunteering and organizing within their own communities because of Huerta.
Deanna Muñoz, founder and president of the Chicano Center for the Arts in Missouri, never met the civil rights icon, but she told The Associated Press that Huerta’s courage, love and sense of purpose live on in people who refuse to be silent.
“She taught generations of Chicanas like me that we don’t have to ask permission to take up space, that our voices matter, and that standing up for our people is never something we should apologize for,” Muñoz posted on social media.
Here’s more reaction to Huerta and her legacy:
US Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, New Mexico Democrat
“At every rally, Dolores Huerta would ask, “Who has the power?” And together, we would roar back, “The people have the power!” She spent her life reminding us that power doesn’t belong to the wealthy or the powerful. It belongs to the people who march, who organize, who vote, who stand up for one another. Dolores may not be here to lead the chant, but her voice will echo through generations. And every time we raise our voices for justice, we will answer her call.”
NAACP President Derrick Johnson
“Dolores Huerta was a guiding light in the struggle for justice, and we know that her legacy will continue to fuel the movement she dedicated her life to. When Dolores turned 21, she celebrated her birthday by registering to vote. As we honor her today and every day, let’s do our part to fight for labor rights, to fight for civil rights, and to make our voices heard at the ballot box. May she rest in peace and power.”
Latino Victory Project president and CEO Katharine Pichardo
“Without Dolores, Latino Victory would not exist — we are eternally grateful to her for breaking barriers and paving the way for Latino civil rights, political power, and Latina activism. She inspired millions, and the best way to honor her memory is to keep advocating for working families and civil rights, and to strengthen Latino political power.”
Former US Interior Secretary Ken Salazar
“Dolores Huerta’s living legacy is her lifelong struggle for justice for the farmworkers who feed our nation. My family and I were honored to work alongside her for more than 50 years, inspired by her leadership and powerful voice across the United States and Mexico. She understood that our diversity is our greatest strength and that together, we can build a more just and inclusive America. In her words, we can change the world for the better: ¡Sí se puede!”

title: Maine GOP chair accuses Jackson campaign of ‘hypocrisy’ over billionaire money
text:
AUGUSTA, Maine (WABI) -Maine GOP Chair Jim Deyermond said at a press conference in Augusta that Troy Jackson claims he does not take money from billionaires or corporate PACs.
Deyermond cited Federal Election Commission records and publications, including Forbes and the conservative Free Beacon, to say Jackson’s campaign has received support from billionaires.
He also said the campaign has coordinated advertising with the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which receives billionaire contributions.
“We’re talking about the hypocrisy of saying he doesn’t get them, when everyone knows he does. And it’s public record. It’s not like you can hide it. It’s public record. And he keeps stating that he’s not. That’s the problem we have,” Deyermond said.
Campaign responds
Jackson’s campaign was asked for comment. Campaign spokesperson Ella McFarlane responded with a statement:
“Nearly 200,000 people have donated to Troy’s campaign, with 95% of contributions under $100, support from Mainers in all 16 counties, and no corporate PACs – unlike Susan Collins who is heavily funded by corporate PACs and wealthy special interests whose bidding she does in Washington. While Susan Collins remains at the center of a pay-for-play scandal where she steered taxpayer dollars to campaign donors, Troy has always been clear that billionaires need to pay their fair share and he’ll always put working people first.”

title: King tides inundate streets and flood homes and businesses along both US coasts
text:
King tides have inundated parts of both U.S. coasts, flooding streets and sending seawater into homes and businesses in beach communities in California, Florida and the Carolinas.
The tides began with the full moon earlier this week and could cause flooding in some areas into the weekend, forecasters said. King tides are caused by the gravitational pull and alignments of the Earth, moon, and sun. They can occur several times a year and last several days.
This week’s king tides have been exacerbated by additional factors, forecasters said Wednesday.
In Florida, strong high pressure to the north and low pressure over the Caribbean were causing increased swells, Chris Fisher, a National Weather Service meteorologist in Miami, said.
Along the California coast, the ongoing super El Niño has warmed the ocean, leading to an increased volume of seawater. Another factor was the occurrence of Kelvin waves, a series of pulses of warm water that lift the sea level, said Roger Gass, a meteorologist with the weather service’s Bay Area forecast office in Monterey.
King tides, like their name, are definitely noticeable. Residents don’t need a beach to see the ocean. The ocean came to them.
In Southern California, Huntington Beach residents placed sandbags outside of homes Wednesday to try to keep floodwaters out. Some people used paddleboards and surfboards to move about the streets. Stretches of the Pacific coast Highway were closed, and tides were expected to approach record levels in Orange and San Diego counties.
In the northern part of the state, minor flooding was expected through Saturday in low-lying areas along shorelines and tidal waterways during peak high tides, the weather service said.
Gass said the coastal flooding generally occurred within 1 1/2 hours before and after high tides, which are peaking 1.9 feet (about a half-meter) above normal in Northern California.
Most of Florida’s Atlantic coast was under flood warnings through early Friday. Street flooding also was reported in South Carolina coastal cities, including Charleston and Myrtle Beach, and rip currents were possible as far north as North Carolina’s Outer Banks.
“It’s been a rough beach week,” Fisher said. “We’ve had a high risk of rip currents and some high surf out there. The beach conditions are going to continue to be rough through the weekend. It’s been a good week to stay out of the water and stay away from the beaches.”
In Fort Lauderdale, Florida, getting to the multiple waterfront venues at what’s billed as the world’s largest-in-water boat show was tricky, requiring driving through flooded streets next to marinas, hotels and convention centers.
Virginia Key, a barrier island in Miami, saw its highest king tide and the third-highest water level since records were first kept going back three decades, Fisher said.
“The only times we’ve seen higher was during hurricanes,” Fisher said. “It’s historical from a king tide perspective.”

title: Canada goose saved after rusty metal ring found lodged in mouth
text:
Canada goose saved after rusty metal ring found lodged in mouth
A Canada goose was released back into the wild in Pennsylvania after officials said it was found with a rusty metal ring lodged inside its mouth.
The Raven Ridge Wildlife Center said the Canada goose, spotted walking along sidewalks in the busy city areas of York, Pennsylvania, needed "immediate assistance" after videos showed the animal was injured.
Upon examination, the wildlife center said a rusty metal ring was stuck around the bottom part of its bill. The object was believed to have been stuck for an extended period of time, causing significant bleeding and discomfort.
Related video: Moose rescued after being stuck in wire
Officials said the goose was also thin and severely dehydrated.
"The ring was removed, but the goose was so weak that it seemed to have lost all will to fight. We cleaned the caked-on blood from its body and checked for any other injuries," Raven Ridge Wildlife Center said. "After being bathed in warm water, the goose began to respond positively, drinking fresh water, floating, and even grooming its matted chest feathers."
The center said the goose has since been cleared and released.
"The goose was very photogenic and clearly felt better to be free again," officials said.

title: The Most Popular Streaming Movies This Week
text:
The Most Popular Movies on Streaming This Week
The world of streaming provides a near-infinite array of viewing possibilities. There are now countless streaming services, each with their own libraries containing hundreds or thousands of movies to watch. (Did you know there’s a streaming called Fawesome? Well, there is. And I have heard its selection is fawesome.)
With all those choices and with all those services, it’s hard to know what people are actually watching. Most streaming services do not share their data, and those who publish “most viewed” lists often do so using arcane mathematical formulas that can’t be fact checked. (Do we really think Hot Wheels Let's Race: Attack of the T-Rex had 5.9 million views on Netflix last week? I mean, I have never even heard of this movie until literally right this very minute, but I have no proof that it didn’t. Maybe it did!)
One way I like to investigate this topic is by looking at streaming films’ popularity on the movie-based social media app Letterboxd. As we have outlined previously, popularity on Letterboxd is determined by “a mix of member activity, including reviews, comments, watches, logs, watchlists, etc.” The more people are reviewing, watching (and saying they want to watch), logging, and writing about something, the higher it rates on the site in terms of “popularity.”
But Letterboxd also allows you to filter results in their database according to where movies are available, either in theaters or on VOD or streaming. And when you weed out the popular films that are exclusively available in theaters, you wind up with a list of the most popular titles of the moment on streaming — and here they are (and where to currently stream them)...

title: Turner-area’s Cari Medd named Superintendent of the Year
text:
Cari Medd, a 33-year veteran educator and administrator, was named 2027 Superintendent of the Year Wednesday for her dedicated leadership and her support of students’ well-being and achievement.
Maine School Superintendent’s Association recognized Medd, superintendent of Maine School Administrative 52 in the Turner area, at the start of the organization’s annual meeting in Augusta.
Medd, of Hebron, has worked to improve student behavior, decrease suspensions, and support students with disabilities. She has long been regarded as an innovative, purpose-driven leader, according to the association’s new release announcing the award.
In 1992-93, Medd taught social studies at Leavitt Area High School in Turner for seven years and coached field hockey. It was her first job after earning her teaching certification and master’s degree from Harvard University.
“I always wanted to be an educator but didn’t major in it in college, so I had to go back to school to be certified and then started my career at Leavitt Area High School,” she wrote in an email.
Before returning to MSAD 52 in 2022, which serves Greene, Leeds and Turner, Medd spent 16 years as the principal of Poland Regional High School. She took a job teaching social studies at the newly built school in 1999. She was recognized twice as a leader in education.
She wrote that she stayed in the field as a superintendent because she loves to “solve problems and work with really smart people who care about their work.”
Medd has led a yearslong strategy to better respond to student behavior needs and improve academic achievement, particularly among students with disabilities, according to the association’s release.
“Through increased training in Positive Behavior Interventions and Support and more education around tobacco and drug use, suspensions in the district have fallen by 45% in recent years,” according to the association.
Under Medd’s leadership, the district has also made a deliberate effort to increase co-teaching and inclusion of students with disabilities into mainstream classroom settings, resulting in substantial improvements in academic growth. Two district elementary schools are partnering with the University of Maine System to increase the amount of time that students with disabilities are spending with non-disabled peers.
“It is every school leader’s dream to work with other outstanding educators and support personnel that stay focused on the important work at hand. It is my honor to work with the high quality operations leaders in our district — facilities, technology, food service, transportation and business office — who work countless hours to support our students, staff and schools,” Medd wrote.
Medd credited the MSAD 52 leadership team’s daily collaboration and dedication to student success, calling her six principals and administrators “rock stars.”
“Cari took a District that had struggled during Covid, had endured years of facility neglect and stagnant review of curriculum and learning standards. Although there is work to do, she has navigated tumultuous community difference, advocated for increased student opportunity and re-ignited focus on curriculum and educational practice. She is dedicated to the change needed in our district while supporting the many wonderful teachers within our community,” Michelle Hathaway wrote in a comment on the MSAD 52 Parent Connection Facebook in response to a Sun Journal request for comment.
Crystal Marie also wrote on the page, “Is our district perfect? No. When Superintendent Medd was hired to our district, I was concerned. She was going to be a brand new superintendent who would need to hire a business manager, a transportation director, a facilities director, and three principals, plus various teaching positions. She has built an incredible team around her and has very high expectations. Again, not everyone will agree, but having a front row seat on the school board for 6 years showed me that Superintendent Medd understands ALL aspects of education, has a deep appreciation for our community, and above all wants to do what is best for the students and staff. She walked into a dumpster fire, frankly. She has proven she can put out multiple fires and absolutely deserves this award. Way to go, Cari!!!!”
Throughout her time as superintendent, Medd has demonstrated an unwavering commitment to the district, defined by a leadership style that is both participative and student-centered,” MSAD 52 Assistant Superintendent Theresa Gillis wrote.
“She provides individualized and group support of her leadership team, is forward thinking in her work, and is committed to ensuring that purposeful improvement happens in all departments,” Gillis wrote.
Beyond the classroom, Medd has also been lauded for her transparency and communication. Through information-gathering and collaboration with community leaders, she has created a more open budget development process incorporating feedback from local residents, according to the release.
“I have known and worked with many school administrators over the years, and I can say without a doubt that Cari is one of the best,” district board Chairman Peter Ricker wrote. “She has performed her duties as a superintendent in the most professional and level-headed manner. As the board chair, I am aware of most of these situations, and I can say that took some doing.”
Ricker commended Medd for remaining focused on student education while professionally navigating complex board and district issues.
Eileen King of the Maine School Superintendents Association praised Medd for her professionalism, strong connections with staff and the community, and leadership in establishing a safe, trusting environment that improves student learning.

title: Rumford clock tower damage connected to stabbing, shootings, and drug trafficking
text:
Historic clock tower in Rumford, Maine, damaged by gunfire
Police in Rumford say they have finally been able to confirm that the clock tower on the historic town municipal building was damaged by apparent gunshots.
The building, which houses the Rumford Police Department, Rumford District Court, Oxford County Sheriff's Office substation, and municipal offices, was first struck on Oct. 10.
A crane was brought in on Wednesday morning and crews were able to observe and document the damage to the clock tower.
On Oct. 10, officers at the Police Department heard multiple gunshots at about 8:42 p.m., including what sounded like something hitting the building.
As police investigated, they also got reports of people reporting shots fired near the intersection of Waldo Street and Rumford Avenue, about a quarter of a mile away, on the other side of the river.
There were more reports of shots fired in the same neighborhood early the next morning and then again on Oct. 14.
Before the sun came up on Oct. 14, police executed a search warrant at 209 Waldo Street, right at the intersection with Rumford Avenue, as part of an ongoing investigation into drug trafficking and weapons offenses. That search ended up prompting a shelter-in-place advisory for Rumford as police looked for Blake Lachance.
Lachance was arrested in Westbrook on Oct. 20, thanks to help from the United States Marshals Service and Westbrook Police. He was charged with one count each of aggravated assault with a dangerous weapon, criminal threatening with a dangerous weapon and reckless conduct with a dangerous weapon in connection with the Oct. 14 incident in Rumford.
On Oct. 25, Rumford Police responded to a double stabbing at the same address, 209 Waldo Street. A 44-year-old man had a knife wound on his back with significant bleeding, and a 37-year-old woman had a knife wound on the side of her abdomen. A 19-year-old man from Lewiston, Jazya Swan, and a 15-year-old girl from Lisbon were both charged with elevated aggravated assault, criminal threatening with a dangerous weapon, and refusing to submit to arrest or detention.
Over the last two weeks, police say they discovered damage consistent with a bullet strike to an elevated part of the Municipal Building's clock tower facing Waldo Street. Due to the height and location of the damage, investigators were unable to safely access the area for a closer examination until the crane was brought in on Wednesday.
Crews are working to make repairs and prevent water from getting in and causing more damage.
Police say the damage is believed to be a result of the reported gunfire.
Law enforcement personnel were inside the building at the time of the Oct. 10 incident, although municipal offices and District Court were closed.
On Oct. 25, Rumford Police responded to a double stabbing at the same address, 209 Waldo Street, resulting in additional arrests and criminal charges.
Rumford Police Chief Tony Milligan said "it is frustrating" to see his community characterized by the criminal actions of a small number of people.
"Those individuals do not define Rumford, and their actions are not a reflection of the overwhelming majority of the good people who live here. "These recent acts of violence are serious, and I fully understand the concerns and frustrations of our residents. They deserve to feel safe in their homes, on their streets, and throughout their community," Milligan said.
"Let me be clear: Enough is enough. We will not allow the reckless and dangerous actions of a few individuals to define our community or undermine the quality of life our residents deserve. Rumford is a good community filled with good people, and we intend to do everything within our lawful authority to keep it that way."
Police said their investigation is ongoing, and there are certain details that are not yet being released.
Anyone with information about the recent gunfire or related violent criminal activity in the Waldo Street area should contact the Rumford Police Department at 207-364-4551.

title: Federal Reserve keeps interest rates unchanged ahead of midterms despite elevated inflation
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Federal Reserve kept its key rate unchanged Wednesday at about 3.9% despite stubbornly high inflation, as Chairman Kevin Warsh suggested its policies are already showing signs of having an impact.
“Inflation remains elevated,” the Fed said in a statement released after its two-day policy meeting. Holding off on an increase will allow “the accumulation of more information” that will help determine what policy the Fed should pursue “to ensure a timely return of inflation” to the central bank’s 2% inflation target, the statement said.
The Fed raised its benchmark rate last month for the first time in three years, defying President Donald Trump’s demands for rate cuts, in an effort to cool inflation more quickly. The Fed is tasked by Congress to combat inflation, and it does so by lifting rates to slow borrowing and spending and reduce price increases.
Michael Reynolds, vice president of investment strategy at Glenmede, a wealth management firm, said the statement suggested the central bank will likely hike its key rate by a quarter-point at its next meeting Dec. 8-9. Wall Street investors now see the odds of an increase then at nearly 85%, according to CME Fedwatch.
“It’s likely going to take one more (hike) from the Fed to get interest rates into restrictive territory,” where they can slow inflation, he said.
The Fed’s decision comes just six days before a midterm election that has focused heavily on concerns around the cost of living and affordability. Consumers have generally soured on an economy weighed down by more expensive gas, groceries, and clothing, among other items. Warsh denied the election played a part in the Fed’s staying pat.
“Politics played no role in the decision,” he said at a news conference following the announcement. “I just spent two days with my colleagues upstairs. I didn’t hear an utterance about politics.”
Warsh faces plenty of challenges in getting inflation back to target. Some of the forces pushing up prices — specifically the rapid buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure and higher energy prices — may not be easily tamed by higher interest rates.
Still, Warsh said the “overwhelming consensus” among Fed officials is what they’ve done “is starting to work some,” noting that credit conditions “tightened for some businesses and households.”
He said specifically that as large tech firms rely more on borrowing to build data centers, higher rates will have a greater ability to cool that investment.
“Do interest rates matter?” Warsh asked. “I believe they do, and I don’t think they’re divorced from the rest of the economy.”
Parts of the economy are being hit by higher rates, which were lifted by market forces, even before the Fed hiked last month. The average 30-year mortgage rate reached a three-year high of 7.4% earlier this month, though it has since slipped a bit. Higher mortgage rates have made buying a home unaffordable for 5 million more Americans since the beginning of the year, according to Oxford Economics, a consulting firm. Over time, Fed rate hikes can make mortgages, auto loans, and credit card borrowing more expensive, adding to Americans’ sense that things like homes and cars are getting pricier.
A separate inflation measure more closely followed by the Fed, the personal consumption expenditures price index, comes out Thursday and is forecast to have jumped 3.6% in September from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August. Core prices, which exclude the food and energy categories, are forecast to have risen 3.1%, up from 3% the previous month. Earlier this month, the consumer price index showed inflation picked up in September, when consumer prices rose 3.7% compared with a year earlier.
Warsh denied that consumers would lose faith in the Fed’s ability to get inflation back to its 2% target, given its decision to forgo a rate hike.
“There is no soft inflation target,” he said.
Two Fed officials dissented from Wednesday’s decision, with Fed governor Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack voting in favor of hiking rates by a quarter point. This is Cook’s first dissent since she was appointed to the board by President Joe Biden in 2022.
Cook has been targeted by the Trump administration, which tried to fire her last year, though the Supreme Court in June ruled she could keep her job while litigation played out. No president has fired a Fed governor before, a sign of the Fed’s longstanding independence from day-to-day politics. Trump renewed his attempt to remove Cook last month by setting up a committee to look into allegations Cook committed mortgage fraud, which she has denied.
President Trump has also slammed the Fed for raising its key rate last month, though he largely blamed the central bank’s rate-setting committee, rather than Warsh, whom he appointed.
The Fed’s policy meeting is part of a busy week for central banks around the world. The Bank of Canada met earlier, and lifted its key rate a quarter point, to 2.5%. Policymakers at the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan are both scheduled to meet Thursday and are expected to keep their key rates unchanged.
For Warsh and the Fed, another key consideration is that the U.S. economy is growing at a healthy pace and unemployment remains low, at 4.2%, even if hiring is also sluggish. Warsh said growth in the July-September quarter likely rose above 3%. That would be up from 2.2% in the April-June quarter.

title: Maine-inspired video game is now ready to play
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
While the shape of the map bears a striking resemblance to Peaks Island, Maine-based game developer Eric Blumrich took inspiration from a number of Casco Bay islands when creating the environment for “Peace Island,” an open-world adventure game in which a player is a cat who wakes up on a remote island to discover all the humans are missing.
What began in 2017 as a bedroom project funded mainly through Kickstarter and later Patreon has morphed into an eight-year endeavor that required Blumrich and his partner, Laura Mackey, to create a video game from the ground up.
But “Peace Island” is decidedly more laid-back than the typical open-world game on the market. At a time when first-person shooter games are popular, Blumrich said they wanted to create something different.
Described by Blumrich as a “cozy,” non-violent game akin to a walking simulator, “Peace Island” is all about discovery and exploration. Players search the island’s abandoned buildings for clues or comb through thousands of pages of books, magazines and letters to piece together the island’s history. Along the way, you’ll run into a whole host of other species such as snails, chickens and deer, each of whom give you missions that advance the story.
“Curl up beneath a blanket, read a book, hang out with cats, and notice something and pursue the story at your own pace,” said Blumrich.
The game is currently in early access on Steam for $15.99, which means the game can be purchased and downloaded, but it hasn’t been completed and may be subject to glitches or bugs. While Blumrich said they are still finding new bugs every day, requiring future patches, he said the game’s operating system is mostly complete and running smoothly.
Currently, 80% of the “Peace Island” game world is available to explore alongside 15 explorable interiors (out of an anticipated 40), a day and night cycle, four playable cats (out of an anticipated nine), 7 non-player character (NPC) species that will give the players missions to complete, and 900 (out of an anticipated 2,000+) pages of books, magazines and letters designed to help the players better understand the game’s story.
However, most of the game’s three-act story is far from complete. Blumrich anticipates that the first act will be completed in the coming weeks, in time for the game’s eighth anniversary on Nov. 17.
Blumrich said there are between 12 and 15 playable missions right now. The missions center on simple objectives such as opening a chicken coop so the island’s chickens can access food, or gathering trash along the beach so a group of snails can play music with it.
“It’s kind of hard to present a vertical slice of the story without giving the entire story away,” said Blumrich. “But if people look around and read a few books and such, they’ll get an inkling of a few things that might be going on.”
Blumrich was secretive about the direction the story would take, to avoid spoiling the eventual story, although he did point out a couple of details worth taking note of.
For example, Blumrich pointed towards a Geiger counter that can be found inside one of the island’s buildings. While the game won’t tell you specifically what to do with the device, Blumrich said that if players bring it to a specific part of the forest, it will make a noise that he said may foreshadow a future direction the story might take.
Blumrich said that he wanted to make the game “as Maine as we can make it,” which includes modeling an in-game religious group after the Shakers, whose last three members live in Maine. At one point, Blumrich had even thrown around the idea of asking Moxie to advertise – something that was ruled out once they learned Moxie had been bought by Coca-Cola back in 2018.
Despite the delays and setbacks that have come about while trying to create an open-world game with a team of two and limited funding, Blumrich said that he and Mackey aren’t giving up.
“I think I can live down the humiliation and betrayal of the audience by being late,” Blumrich said, “but I can’t really make up for the betrayal of just giving up.”

title: 'Banana hero' goes viral after woman dressed in costume calls 911
text:
Woman dressed in banana costume calls 911 after car crashes into bar | Bar searching for its 'banana hero' goes viral
A Florida woman is going viral after calling 911 while dressed in a banana costume.
Stephanie Oropeza and her fiancé were going home from a Halloween party when they witnessed the crash at The Moderne bar on Colonial Drive around 4 a.m. Saturday.
“I yelled at my fiancé. I was like, ‘You need to stop the car right now,’” Oropeza told sister station WESH. “And then we start running, and I’m on the phone with 911.”
The car slammed through tables, umbrellas and a fence outside the bar. The building itself was not damaged and no injuries were reported.
Oropeza did not realize surveillance cameras had captured her running toward the scene in the bright yellow costume.
“The last thing that would have occurred to me is that there was a surveillance camera and that the next day I’d wake up to ‘Banana Hero,’” she said.
The Moderne posted the surveillance video on social media while trying to identify the costumed caller. Management offered her a dinner as a thank-you.
The last-minute Halloween costume quickly turned Oropeza into a viral sensation. Oropeza said she has barely taken off the costume since Saturday and is enjoying her newfound fame.
Still, she hopes the attention highlights a more important lesson.
“I genuinely feel like I just did something that I hope most people do when you see someone in need — just help them out and call who you need to call so they can get the help they need,” Oropeza said. “Despite knowing them or not, despite being in a costume or not.”
Oropeza said the driver of the vehicle stayed at the scene and cooperated with police.
Management at The Moderne said it is also creating a banana-flavored specialty cocktail in Oropeza’s honor. The drink is expected to be added to the menu this week.

title: AARP NEWS YOU CAN USE: AARP Top Concerns for Voters 50-Plus
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
by Joyce Bucciantini
AARP Maine Community Outreach Volunteer
The November elections are rapidly approaching and absentee voting has already started. Historically, Maine has a very high voter turnout rate. According to U.S. Census Bureau data, voters over age 65 vote at higher rates than their younger counterparts. Maine voters age 50-plus show up to vote at higher rates than any other age group, casting 59.3% of all votes in the 2024 general election. Maine’s voters age 50-plus are not shy about making their voices heard at the ballot box and their votes make a difference. In fact, 87% of Maine voters age 50-plus say they are extremely motivated to vote this year.
AARP Maine’s statewide voter survey, released on October 1, examined the issues driving Maine voters as they head toward Election Day. The poll found that concerns about household affordability continue to dominate voters’ minds. Rising prices and the increasing cost of everyday necessities are putting pressure on family budgets, particularly for older Mainers living on fixed incomes. Utility costs emerged as a major concern, with 97% of Maine voters age 50-plus saying it is important for elected officials to ensure utility costs remain affordable.
Voters are also focused on the cost of health care, prescription drugs, housing, food, and fuel. These are not abstract policy debates. They are real-life concerns affecting families and communities across our state. Talk to just about anybody you know in Maine and odds are they will have similar worries about making ends meet in an increasingly expensive world.
Protecting Social Security and Medicare remains one of the most important issues for voters age 50-plus. We all pay into these programs during our working careers and expect them to be there when we need them. The AARP Maine survey found that more than 93% of voters age 50-plus are more likely to support candidates who will protect Social Security from cuts. Any reductions to Social Security or Medicare would have serious consequences for many older Mainers and their household budgets.
The survey also highlighted the challenges facing Maine’s family caregivers and aging population. Eighty-five percent of voters age 50-plus say they are more likely to support candidates who advocate for unpaid family caregivers, while 94 percent say it is important for elected officials to increase home- and community-based services that help older adults remain independent as they age. These findings reflect the reality that many Maine families are balancing work, caregiving responsibilities, and rising costs all at the same time.
While voters may disagree on many issues and candidates, the October survey sends a clear message. Maine’s voters age 50-plus want leaders who will address affordability, protect Social Security and Medicare, support family caregivers, and help older adults remain independent. As Election Day approaches, candidates would be wise to listen. Maine’s largest voting bloc is paying attention.
As always, check out the AARP website for an AARP event near you. I also urge you to visit www.aarp.org/votesME, our voter engagement hub, where you’ll find helpful information about our priority issues, Q and A with the candidates and much more.
Joyce Bucciantini is a retired middle school educator. She currently coordinates Delta Kappa Gamma’s Read to Me program, is a tutor with Literacy Volunteers-Androscoggin, and is an active AARP Maine volunteer. She enjoys her gardens, being outdoors and traveling.

title: Parents say students were forced to get off school bus and walk 3 miles home on dangerous roads
text:
GUNTOWN, Miss. (WTVA/Gray News) — Parents in Mississippi are demanding answers after they said their 11-year-old daughter’s school bus driver told her to get off the bus and walk miles home.
James and Ann Lofton said their child and several other kids were forced to walk three miles to get home, though it’s unclear why.
“You put your children out to catch the bus, you expect them to be safe on the bus,” Ann Lofton said. “You expect them to get to school safely, you expect them to get home safely, and then you get a phone call [saying] they’re walking down the side of the road. How is that keeping them safe?”
The parents said they reported the incident to the Lee County School District. The Loftons said Superintendent Coke Magee suspended the driver for five days after the complaint.
“We are aware of this, and it is being handled as a personnel issue,” the Lee County School District said in a statement.
James Lofton said he wants everyone involved to lose their jobs.
“That’s bull. It is bull crap. I think all their jobs, the superintendent, the one over the buses. I think they all need to be fired,” James Lofton said. “Because they’re hired to keep our kids safe. Instead, they put them out on the side of the road.”
James Lofton took his concerns to law enforcement. Lee County Sheriff Jim Johnson said investigators have not found evidence to support criminal charges against the driver.
The Loftons are now seeking a lawyer as they consider their options.
“I’m not only protecting my kids by doing this. I’m protecting your kid, the neighbor’s kid, and the kid down the street,” James Lofton said. “What happens when one of these kids gets killed? I will take action, as in the court of law. Because it’s not just my kid. It’s the community’s kids.”

title: FEC campaign finance filings website experiences outage ahead of midterm elections
text:
Federal Election Commission campaign finance filings site has outage ahead of midterms
The Federal Election Commission’s electronic filing system is experiencing an outage that started late Monday, and it continued throughout the day Tuesday — one week ahead of the midterm elections.
Related video above: Are electronic voting machines "flipping" votes? Experts say no.
The FEC, which enforces campaign finance rules but does not oversee how elections are conducted, in a status update at 8:17 p.m. ET Tuesday stated that "The issue has been identified and a fix is being implemented." However, the FEC, on its website and social media pages, as of late Tuesday night, hadn't given further details about what the problem was or how it was being fixed by IT personnel.
As of 11:50 p.m. ET Tuesday, the FEC's website still stated, "FEC's electronic filing system is currently offline: We apologize for the inconvenience, and we’re continuing to work to resolve the issue."
CNN reports that the outage affects candidates' and committees' ability to file campaign finance reports that detail last-minute contributions and spending on specific contests, but that the outage does not affect voting in the midterms currently underway across the country, CNN reports.
The website for searching already-filed reports remains online, a spokesperson told the Associated Press. He declined to elaborate on the outage.
This is a developing story. Check back for updates

title: Did You Know Sugarland Was Originally a Trio?
text:
Did You Know Sugarland Was Originally a Trio?
The country group behind hits like “Baby Girl” and “Stuck Like Glue” started out as a trio before becoming the duo fans know today.
👇 KEEP READING: 68 Artists Not in the Country Music Hall of Fame 👇
Sugarland formed in the Atlanta area in 2002 as a trio featuring Jennifer Nettles, Kristian Bush and Kristen Hall.
Hall played guitar, sang harmony and helped write songs for the group’s 2004 debut album, “Twice the Speed of Life,” which included the hits “Baby Girl” and “Something More.”
She left in late 2005, and Nettles and Bush announced her departure in January 2006, saying she wanted to stay home and focus on songwriting.
Nettles and Bush continued together, releasing their second album, “Enjoy the Ride,” later that year.
Sugarland is celebrating the 20th anniversary of “Enjoy the Ride” with the 2026 Ride or Die Tour, featuring hits and fan favorites from the duo’s catalog.
The tour will stop at the Cross Insurance Center in Bangor on Nov. 11, with special guest Payton Sullivan.
And there you have it! Sugarland’s familiar two-person lineup took shape just before the release of one of the group’s best-known albums.

title: Building community at the Brunswick tree festival
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
It’s hard to believe that we are only about three weeks away from the Merrymeeting Tree Fest. We could really use your help. “Who, me?” you ask. Yes, you.
Whether you are a new community member, a seasoned community member, a business, a nonprofit, a municipal employee, a student, an adult, retired, or any combination of these things, there is something you can do to help us with this huge community event. This is a new festival, and with that comes some new opportunities to overcome challenges, which makes your participation even more worth it.
Here is a list, in convenient Q&A form, because Q&A form is just more fun:
What is the Merrymeeting Tree Fest?
This is a tree festival in which businesses and local groups of any kind build tree spaces with different themes and gifts, and they get raffled off the weekend before Thanksgiving and after. Over the six days hundreds of families will attend to try to win a tree, but also to create children’s crafts, enjoy live entertainment, meet Santa, and so much more.
Where and when is the Merrymeeting Tree Fest?
The Merrymeeting Tree Fest will be Nov. 20-22 and Nov. 27-29 at the Brunswick Landing Y.
Isn’t there already a tree festival in Brunswick?
The chamber used to be a part of a different tree festival, but this is a brand new one, with new partners, in a new location — so it’s a new name too. However, there will be some similar aspects as pretty much each of the dozen or more tree festivals in the state, run basically the same way. It’s kind of like a golf tournament — they all have their own unique things, but every golf tournament in the state is also pretty similar.
Who are the partners for the Merrymeeting Tree Fest?
This is a fundraising event where proceeds are split between the Bath-Brunswick-Topsham Regional Chamber and the Brunswick Landing Y (the host site). Additionally, there is a way for many nonprofits to make a little money too — see below.
Well, you can’t just leave that hanging — tell us about the nonprofit moneymaking thing!
OK! So, this year we are instituting paid volunteerism where, when you sign up for a shift, you can ask for a donation for your time spent volunteering to go to the local nonprofit of your choice. The amount is $30 per shift.
What does volunteering entail?
A lot of things, but mostly greeting people, and for some roles, handling money transactions. We have 11 volunteers per shift (mostly two hours, last shift daily is 2.5 hours). We have two stations for tree ticket sales, and one station for 50/50 tickets, entry table, mobile assistants (help where needed) and one craft volunteer. You also get a T-shirt!
You mentioned ‘new challenges’ — what does that mean?
Well, it means two things: The first is we really need help getting the word out. Yes, we have sponsors to do some media, and we will have road signs, but we need to spread the word far and wide. Following the Merrymeeting Tree Fest Facebook page is a great way to stay up to date and we encourage people to share it with friends. We are beginning daily Facebook updates by Nov. 1. For flyers and more information, check out MidcoastMaine.com.
Secondly, we need decorations! The Brunswick Landing Y is an incredible venue, but we need a lot of holiday cheer to make it feel as festive as can be.
Did you swap out your outdoor lights from colored lights to white lights? We will take the extra lights! Did you buy an inflatable or lawn display that is just a pain in the butt and you want to get rid of it? Reach out to me! Do you have a fake tree or wreath you don’t display anymore and is taking up space in storage? Excellent! Do you have displays you set up at home, but you would let us borrow it for the weekends around Thanksgiving because you decorate after Dec. 1? Great!
We will gradually build up a slew of decorations in the coming years, but if you have something we could have, or borrow, please email [email protected].
How else can we get involved?
Loaded question, but here we go:
Get a tree space: Costs nothing to register and you need to put only $500 worth of value in the space plus a fake tree. Any business, organization, group, family or individual can sign up — great exposure!
Nonprofits: Get promotion by creating a door prize wreath!
Donate an item: If you are a business and have items or gift cards to showcase, we will find a tree space to put them on. Or if you are individual and want to donate a gas gift card, or give a handmade sweater, or a piece of art, we would love that too. Again, email [email protected] if interested.
Tell a friend, invite them to join you: Everyone wants something to do, and we intentionally make this affordable. Heck, the raffle tickets are just 50 cents apiece, and the entry to get in is by suggested donation, so anyone can come in.
In closing, this is an opportunity to build community through our actions. If you want to donate to, say, Mid Coast Hunger Prevention Program, but you don’t have the extra cash, come volunteer for two shifts some afternoon and we will donate $60 to them on your behalf.
Want to help but don’t have the time? Let us borrow your lawn display for a couple of weekends.
Or just show up. With family, friends, grandkids. If you’re an entertainer, we have performance spots open. However, you want to help build community, I think we can find a way to engage you in this great event. Reach out — I’d love to chat with you about it.
Cory King is executive director of the Bath-Brunswick-Topsham Regional Chamber of Commerce.

title: Troy Jackson’s closing campaign message is here
text:
Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Troy Jackson is making his final pitch to voters about why they should oust five-term Republican incumbent Susan Collins, framing the race as a choice between Trump-aligned billionaires and ordinary working Mainers.
The closing days of the race have devolved into an onslaught of personal attacks and negative ads, fueled largely by outside groups aligned with Collins. Republican-aligned groups have attacked Jackson’s family and questioned whether he has “the tools” to be a senator. A recent ad from the Collins campaign spotlighted the moment Jackson told her to “shut up” at an October debate.
“As much as Susan Collins and her billionaire backers want you to think I’m the bogeyman, I’m not,” Jackson said in op-ed published in the Bangor Daily News. “I’m just a working guy who’s tired of working Mainers being ignored.”
The 58-year-old also published an op-ed on the Portland Press Herald website on Wednesday in which he laid out what he said were the generational stakes of the Senate race. Jackson’s article seemed directed especially toward women: He wrote about his newborn granddaughter, the closure of birthing centers and the fall of Roe v. Wade after Collins voted to confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the U.S. Supreme Court.
The op-eds dovetailed with his final campaign ad of the season, in which he says “Mainers will decide the direction of the whole country.”
In addition to bashing Jackson, Collins has focused her campaign’s closing days on the amount of federal dollars she brings to Maine as chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee. She often notes that she’s delivered $1.5 billion to the state over the last five years.
On Monday, Collins visited a mobile home park in Camden that received a $1.3 million federal earmark to help upgrade its sewer system.
The contrast in closing messages shows how Democrats have been trying to nationalize the race, while Republicans have sought to focus on local issues. Both sides also appear to be making a final push for the same constituency: moderate women.
In a radio interview on WVOM on Wednesday, Collins noted that President Donald Trump only has two years left on his term, while whoever wins the Senate race next week will serve six years. She said voters should consider who can best help to “fix some of the problems created by this administration.”
“It’s not going to ever be Troy Jackson,” Collins said. “I’m going to be the fifth-highest ranking senator if I’m elected. Troy would be number 100, or if he’s lucky, 99. The difference that you can make for the people of Maine, because of your seniority, is enormous.”
Collins has come under attack by Jackson and Democratic-aligned groups for what they say are her moves to aid Trump’s agenda: voting to confirm conservative justices to the Supreme Court, passing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and launching a war with Iran, which has fueled inflation and high gas prices. (Collins did not support early, Democratic-led efforts to revoke Trump’s war powers in Iran, but she voted against the war nine times after the 60-day threshold for congressional approval had been reached under the War Powers Act.)
The 73-year-old has also been accused of corruption — charges aided by a ProPublica investigation about a possible pay-to-play scheme with a defense contractor. And her husband’s work as a former lobbyist and his stock portfolio have also been in the spotlight.
In a statement, Collins’ campaign stayed on the attack, criticizing Jackson for what it characterized as his broken pledge to not take money from political action committees.
“In the final week of this campaign, Senator Collins will be crisscrossing the state on her All of Maine bus tour, highlighting her record of independent leadership and delivering results for Maine,” campaign spokesperson Blake Kernen said in a statement.
In his Bangor Daily News op-ed, Jackson called the federal funding Collins touts a pittance compared to the damage she has enabled during Trump’s second term. He highlighted Collins’ vote to advance the One Big Beautiful Bill, which contained $1 trillion in healthcare cuts and extended tax cuts for the wealthy, though Collins ultimately voted against the bill.
“I think this campaign boils down to Susan Collins and the billionaires versus the people of Maine,” he wrote. “Collins has spent the last 30 years in Washington. I think she’s been there too long and she’s become part of the problem.”
Democrats see Maine as a prime pickup opportunity, since Collins is the only Senate Republican running in a state won by Democrats in the 2024 presidential election. But Collins has proved resilient in the past, surviving a tough reelection battle in 2020, despite trailing in the polls.
Jackson has enlisted a roster of national surrogates in the closing weeks. Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., a possible 2028 presidential candidate, held a rally in Freeport on Tuesday night and had additional events planned in Brunswick on Wednesday. His visit came on the heels of appearances by Sens. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.
Last week, Collins’ campaign received a boost from former Sen. Joe Manchin, a longtime former Democrat-turned-independent from West Virginia. Manchin touted Collins’ independence and bipartisan chops during stops in Androscoggin County.

title: New spin for old propeller
text:
They say everything comes around again and so it is with an old propeller that for some of us has a bit of fond nostalgia attached to it. As recently reported in this newspaper, Wiscasseter Steve Erskine has offered to take a turn at restoring the propeller that once pushed the steamboat Winter Harbor up and down the Sheepscot River from Wiscasset to Boothbay Harbor. Left to the mercy of the elements for many years, Mother Nature has slowly eaten away at the propeller’s four cast iron blades. But maybe this time something will finally be done to preserve this maritime relic from the steam age. I’ve known Steve a long time; if anyone can see this project through he can.
You could say Steve is one of those Mainers who has saltwater in his blood. He’s a 40-year member of Wiscasset Yacht Club, and has owned many boats over the years including a Friendship sloop he continues to sail. He recently retired after working 42 years at Bath Iron Works. Much of his career was spent in welding/engineering, although in recent years his responsibilities at the Bath shipyard included serving as a tugboat captain. After they've been launched the tugs guide the newly built Naval ships into the Kennebec River. Steve’s also one of the volunteer captains of the Virginia. That’s the floating classroom and living museum built by volunteers of Maine’s First Ship, a non-profit group also based in Bath where the vessel is berthed.
Steve has a personal interest in preserving the propeller. “My granddad, Roy B. Rowe, was the last captain of the Winter Harbor, so me seeing the propeller preserved is a bit personal. It also serves as a link to our town’s past. I think it would be wonderful to have it properly preserved and put on display at the waterfront.” Steve hopes to involve Bath Iron Works in the preservation project. “They’ve got the means and expertise to do a permanent restoration of the propeller. They’d have ideas too, how best to mount it after the work is finished.”
The story of the Winter Harbor began over a hundred years ago in the early 1900s. In those times coastal Maine was still greatly dependent on the water because there were very few paved roads. The fastest way to travel from Wiscasset to the communities on the Boothbay peninsula was by water. One of the boats that routinely made the trip was the Winter Harbor, a small steamboat nicknamed, “Old Reliable” for its reputation of always being on time.
About 35 years ago Jim Sutter, Wiscasset’s harbor master, suggested I write a newspaper story about the Winter Harbor. Jim put me in touch with Maurice Caton who worked as a laborer for the town’s highway department. (Both Mr. Sutter and Mr. Caton have long since passed away.) In hindsight, I think Jim was hoping something might be done about saving the boat’s propeller that had been stashed behind the town garage for safekeeping. I’ll get to how that happened in a minute. When I interviewed him, Maurice told me he’d been aboard the Winter Harbor dozens of times when he was a boy.
“My Uncle Mark used to work as a deckhand on her,” he said, adding the Winter Harbor used to make three trips a day back and forth from Wiscasset to Boothbay Harbor. Along with mail, the boat carried freight, passengers and the latest news.
For many years the Winter Harbor provided a good living for its owner and skipper Captain Frank Rowe, but like all steam-driven vessels, her fate was sealed with the arrival of the early automobiles and better roads. In 1927, the Winter Harbor’s ownership suffered a financial blow when they lost the mail contract. Harder times were to come during the years of the Great Depression. Unable to adapt to the changing economy the Winter Harbor was soon left abandoned at the Wiscasset waterfront. One day the junkmen arrived and stripped her of her brass, copper and anything else of value. The vandals then had their way, climbing aboard and wreaking havoc. After that she mysteriously sank tied at the pier.
Maurice Caton thought the boat went down in the spring of 1933. He remembered it was March, a bitterly cold day, windy, with cakes of ice along the shoreline. “One day I went to school and on the way home I saw she had gone down,” he said. For years after she sank, Maurice said you could clearly see the boat’s wheelhouse poking out of the water at low tide. Over time only her skeletal wood frame and boiler were visible under the water.
The Winter Harbor was pretty much forgotten until 1978, when one morning a team of divers showed up at the waterfront to explore what remained of the wreck, a diving club as Jim Sutter recalled. Whether it was a training exercise, or just something to do, the divers found and cut off the boat’s four-blade iron propeller. “Hacksawed right through the 4-inch shaft,” Jim told me, after which he said he hoisted it ashore using Wiscasset Yacht Club’s mooring puller. The divers apparently had no interest in keeping the propeller, which sat on the yacht club lawn a while before being hauled off to the town’s highway garage on Hodge Street. It sat behind the garage alongside a pile of old storm drains and other discarded junk until Maurice Caton unearthed the rusting relic for me to photograph for my newspaper story.
After that the propeller underwent its first restoration. Layers of loose rust were removed and a rust inhibitor applied. The propeller was then coated with several layers of paint, silver Rust-Oleum. The talk then was to put it on display at the waterfront near the flag pole with an informational plaque telling its story. After the restoration the propeller was taken to the waterfront, stowed away in the building there and soon forgotten about. In the early 2000s a portion of the Winter Harbor’s rusted round boiler was still visible underwater at low tide. It’s gone now, pulled out and deposited at the town’s landfill when work was done on the pier.
There was renewed interest in saving the propeller in 2011. Rick Lang, a former Wiscasset code enforcement officer, told me Frank Rowe, the owner and skipper of the Winter Harbor, had been his great-grandfather on his mother’s side. He said after Frank Rowe passed away, his sons Clarke and Roy took over ownership of the Winter Harbor and piloted the boat.
Lang said the front cover of The Rudder Magazine, dated March 1940, featured a picture of the sunken Winter Harbor. The pilothouse and bow are shown sticking up out of the water just as Maurice Caton described it. As to her sinking, Rick surmised once the boat’s boilers went cold there was no way to keep the water out of the bilges. He said no attempt was made to raise her because times were hard and money scarce. “Because she was a coal-burner, there was no value to her other than scrap,” he said.
According to Lang, the Winter Harbor was initially built to provide passenger and freight service between the villages of Bar Harbor and Winter Harbor, her namesake. After proving too small for her owners, she was put up for sale. In 1906 Captain Frank Rowe of Boothbay came to be in possession of her. After he passed away in 1925, Captain Roy B. Rowe took over the day-to-day operation of the steamboat, assisted by his brother Clarke Rowe. All of the Rowes lived at or near Boothbay Harbor. Lang told me the Winter Harbor’s schedule coincided with the arrival of the eastbound train of Maine Central Railroad’s Rockland branch. The Winter Harbor continued its Boothbay-Wiscasset run after losing the mail contract, but not for long; the boat’s last run was in 1932.
Along with the Winter Harbor’s propeller Steve hopes BIW might restore several of the old iron pieces salvaged from the old Wiscasset schooners, Hesper and Luther Little. These include the iron bollards, hawse pipes and capstan all of which can be found at the waterfront.
Phil Di Vece earned a B.A. in journalism studies from Colorado State University and an M.A. in journalism at the University of South Florida. He is the author of three Wiscasset books and is a frequent news contributor to the Boothbay Register/Wiscasset Newspaper. He resides in Wiscasset and be contacted at news@wiscassetnewspaper.com

title: Girls and boys earn trip to state meet
text:
The Boothbay Region High School/Wiscasset Middle High School girls and boys cross-country teams qualified for next week’s State Meet by finishing high at the Southern Maine Class C Regional Championships on Saturday, Oct. 24.
According to coach Nick Scott, the girls' team, seeded 5th, finished as runners-up, while the boys, who needed to place at least 7th to continue the long-running streak of qualifying for states, were able to secure a 7th-place finish.

Twin Brooks isn't a PR course, so for anyone close to their personal best, it was a really good day.”

title: Rays' 12th-inning rally stuns Brewers, forces Game 5
text:
Rays stun Brewers with 2-run 12th-inning rally to force Game 5 in Tampa Bay
Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night that forced Game 5.
Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th as Milwaukee neared a sweep and its first World Series title.
Related video above: Brewers fans break merchandise sales records during World Series
But the Rays, also seeking their first championship, rallied in the bottom half after a throwing error by third baseman Joey Ortiz on Junior Caminero's leadoff grounder against reliever Antonio Senzatela.
Liam Hicks singled off Shane Drohan, who relieved in his first appearance since Oct. 15, and DeLuca's single to center drove in pinch-runner Cedric Mullins to tie the score at 3.
Chandler Simpson's single loaded the bases and Milwaukee employed a five-man infield with the infield in.
Williamson, who had been 1 for 15 in the postseason, hit a chopper over first baseman Jake Bauers and into right field.
Game 5 will be Wednesday night at Tropicana Field.
Tampa Bay became just the fifth of 26 teams that fell behind 3-0 in the World Series to win Game 4. The previous four lost Game 5.
Of 43 teams to trail 3-0 in any best-of-seven postseason matchup, the only one that rebounded to win was the Boston Red Sox against the New York Yankees in the 2004 American League Championship Series.

title: Passing truck sends SUV off Maine road and into a camper
text:
A passing pickup truck sent an SUV off the road and into a camper in Sidney on Wednesday morning.
Libby Ramsay Boucher, 18, of Augusta was driving a 2018 Ford F-150 on West River Road, near Ferry Road, about 6:42 a.m. when Boucher tried to overtake a 2023 Subaru Outback at a corner, according J. Chris Read, chief deputy of the Kennebec County Sheriff’s Office.
But another vehicle was oncoming as Boucher tried to pass the Subaru, and the pickup truck and SUV “came into contact” and the Subaru, driven by 48-year-old David Worthing of Sidney, went off the road, hit a culvert, demolished a camper and came to a rest on its front grill perpendicular to the ground, Read said.
Firefighters had to free Worthing from the totaled Subaru. The Ford had just minor scrapes and a flat tire.
Worthing was taken to the hospital, where he was treated for minor injuries. Boucher wasn’t injured.
No charges have been filed.

title: Son indicted in mother’s death; medical staff say she had feces, insects in hair
text:
TUSCALOOSA COUNTY, Ala. (WBRC/Gray News) - A man has been indicted on charges related to the death of his mother in Alabama.
Jonathan Chad Simmons faces one count of manslaughter and one count of second-degree elder abuse in the death of his mother, according to Tuscaloosa County court documents obtained by WBRC.
The court documents referred to the victim as Jonathan Chad Simmons’ mother, Brenda Hallman Simmons.
Deputies found woman unresponsive
Tuscaloosa County deputies and medical personnel were called to the 13000 block of Alabama Highway 216 on May 16. Law enforcement found Brenda Hallman Simmons, 76, alive but unresponsive.
Brenda Simmons died several days later while receiving medical care. The autopsy revealed she died from sepsis due to complications from multiple open bedsores.
Joint investigation begins
The Tuscaloosa Violent Crimes Unit and the state medical examiner’s office began a joint investigation after the family and health personnel suspected neglect.
According to medical staff at the hospital, Simmons had multiple open wounds and sores on her body and showed signs of not being bathed. She had feces and insects in her hair.
When investigators executed a search warrant at the residence Simmons shared with her adult son, Jonathan Simmons, they found it “excessively dirty and unsanitary.”
Son’s statements to investigators
Jonathan Simmons told investigators he was the custodian and caretaker of his mother. He admitted to being aware of her medical issues, including open wounds and bedsores.
“He stated that he had not taken her to a doctor in over a year,” Jack Kennedy, with the Tuscaloosa Violent Crimes Unit, said.
Charges outlined in indictment
The indictment accuses Jonathan Simmons of recklessly causing his mother’s death by abusing and neglecting an elderly person. It also alleges the abuse or neglect caused his mother serious physical injury.
Jonathan Simmons is being held in the Tuscaloosa County Jail with a $30,000 bond.

title: Maine's Job Market Is Booming, According to New National Rankings
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Maine’s Job Market Is Booming, According to New National Rankings
Maine is once again among the nation's leading states in a category that matters to every single one of us: jobs. That's the kind of news I never get tired of hearing.
WalletHub, a personal finance website, recently published its annual report of the best and worst states for jobs.
How Does Maine Stack up With the Rest of the Country for its Job Market?
Maine came in with an impressive 7th-place ranking, a very strong showing. It was also good enough to make Maine the second-highest-ranked state in New England, with only New Hampshire finishing higher, in 5th place.
Maine’s overall jobs score was 59.66. The scoring is based on a 100-point system divided into two major categories: Job Market and Economic Environment. These categories were further broken down into 34 subcategories to make the analysis as detailed as possible.
Maine ranked 29th in economic environment, likely brought down by subcategories such as commute-friendly jobs and average starting salaries, areas that aren’t necessarily the state’s strongest.
However, Maine bounced back with an incredible 4th-place ranking in the job market category, which includes factors like job opportunities, unemployment rate, and job security.
It’s great to see our state thrive in this category. It's a wonderful testament to both employers and employees. The workforce is strong, my friends. We should all be proud.
What are the Best New England States for Jobs?
As mentioned above, Maine was joined in the top 10 by New Hampshire. But, what about the rest? Here’s how the region stacked up:

title: Brewer City Council bans needle exchange programs
text:
BREWER, Maine (WABI) - The Brewer City Council voted unanimously Tuesday to prohibit needle exchange programs at both fixed and mobile sites in the city.
The council made the change through an amendment to the land use ordinance.
The vote followed public comments from Brewer residents who spoke against syringe service programs. Many said allowing the programs could lead to negative results.
Many residents pointed across the river to Bangor as an example of what they do not want their community to become.
“I think a service location could attract increased foot traffic, loitering, and public drug use. We’ve seen it all in Bangor. Bangor is having huge problems,” one resident said.
Brewer Mayor Jenn Morin said the council considered input from the police chief and residents.
“I think listening to our Chief of Police and then also having conversations with constituents enabled this council body to feel comfortable that we were making a decision that our community endorses,” Morin said.
A six-month ban was proposed in Bangor earlier this year. Brewer is the first neighboring community to pass a ban like this.

title: St. Andrews Auxiliary Thrift Shop finds the home for tiny piece of Harbor history
text:
When I walked into the Boothbay Region Historical Society a few weeks ago, I was hoping that Society President, Kay Wilder, might be able to tell me a little something about the delicate, hand painted porcelain pitcher I had just found in one of the boxes dropped off at the St. Andrews Auxiliary Thrift Shop. And perhaps the Society might want it or know of an organization that would. To my surprise, when I lifted it out of the bubble wrap, Kay’s face immediately lit up and she said, “Oh my, we don’t have that one.” She turned and walked across the hall to a built-in china cabinet where dozens of similar small turn-of-the-century china objects were on display.
None of us were around to enjoy the The Menawarmet Hotel which stood on Atlantic Avenue (where the former Griffin and Harris Law Office now sits) from 1889-1913 when it burned down. And according to my research, high-end resorts during this time period would often gift their affluent guests with small tokens of thanks. In the case of the Menawarmet, it was this little Austrian porcelain pitcher with a transfer print of the hotel exterior and hand painted gold trim.
So, what is the message of this lovely small story of finding the home for this charming treasure? It is that every time we open a bag or go through a bin, we see every single thing you donate as an item that came from a person or family that has its quiet memories and connections to that piece (or sometimes not—the contents of a dumped sock drawer, knitting yarn or a jigsaw puzzle you finally gave up on, etc.). But the bottom line is that you honor us by putting those items in our hands so they have a best second (or more) life in someone else’s home or closet. Please know that we, the hard-working St. Andrews Auxiliary volunteers, so love all the support we get from you, our community, through both your donations and your purchases. At the end of the day, the shop income allows us the ability to fund both scholarships in health fields and directly support needs in our regional healthcare community.
But, every once in a while, as in this case with a tiny porcelain object (that I swear looks like a watering can), you don’t even think about pricing. You already know it has a home, and you can just make sure it gets there.

title: Bangor Councilors vote to end Zoom public comment
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - Zoom public comment for Bangor City Council meetings is officially a thing of the past.
Councilors voted 6 to 2 Monday night to stop offering Zoom participation.
Councilor Susan Faloon who introduced the order said since Zoom participation resumed in January after a brief pause, there has only been one instance where a resident meaningfully participated in comment and was not disruptive. She added the city is not legally obligated to allow virtual comments.
Those who opposed the order said if councilors are permitted to join via Zoom, residents should be permitted the same accommodation.
Faloon added that anyone who cannot attend due to medical reason should contact the city and ask for an accommodation.
You can still comment in person in council chambers and submit a written comment ahead of time.
Councilors Joe Leonard and Wayne Mallar voted against the order. Councilor Daniel Carson was not in attendance.

title: Man loses more than $4,000 after scammers spoof father’s number, claim parents are at gunpoint
text:
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. (KPHO/Gray News) - A man lost thousands of dollars after getting a call that appeared to come from his father’s phone number, with a stranger claiming his parents were being held at gunpoint.
Curtis Indyke was asleep around 11:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 when he got a call that appeared to be from his dad, who lives in Virginia. Indyke lives in Arizona.
“I answer the phone and it’s not my dad. It’s some other male saying he has my parents basically at gunpoint,” Indyke said.
The caller told him to pay or his parents would be shot.
While still on the phone, Indyke said he texted 911 to report his parents were being held hostage in Virginia. The person who claimed to be holding Indyke’s parents hostage continued making threats. In a panic, Indyke sent more than $4,000 through Apple Pay to two separate phone numbers.
“And they also wanted $1,000 worth of crypto gift cards, which I’ve never even heard of. I’m in IT and I’ve never even heard of them,” Indyke said.
Indyke said his bank blocked that purchase.
After the call ended, Indyke called his dad’s number back, but no one answered.
“But then I got scared because, what if the guy had his phone still?” Indyke said.
Police in Virginia later went to Indyke’s parents’ home for a welfare check and they were safe.
“I mean, everybody was just shocked about it,” Indyke said.
Dawn Alexander, a network specialist for AARP Arizona, said the scammers followed a known playbook.
“It feels like there’s an uptick,” Alexander said. “What they’re trying to do is get you in a heightened state for you to react. Spoofing is a very dangerous game right now because it could be anyone from a scammer saying they’re with Medicare, with your hospital, you name it.”
Indyke said Nancy Guthrie’s disappearance immediately came to mind. She is the mother of “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie.
“Especially in Arizona, we know unfortunately about Nancy, the terrible case of Nancy Guthrie. You know, that was my first thought, is, ‘Oh my God, is this happening to me now?’” Indyke said.
Indyke has advice to anyone who might be a victim of a similar scam.
“You need to take a second, pause before you react. You need to think about it, and the safest thing to do is to hang up and call whoever they say that they have,” Indyke said.
Indyke said the $4,000 payment is still pending and that he plans to file a fraud claim once it clears in hopes of getting his money back.
Alexander said these scams used to target primarily older adults, but with artificial intelligence, anyone can become a victim.

title: Brewers relief pitcher breaks postseason record
text:
Brewers relief pitcher Aaron Ashby breaks postseason record
Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Aaron Ashby broke Andrew Miller's record for scoreless innings by a reliever in one postseason with a 1-2-3 ninth in Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday night.
Ashby followed with a scoreless 10th and hasn't allowed a run in 17 2/3 innings in nine postseason appearances. Milwaukee was tied 2-2 with Tampa Bay going into the 11th inning.
Related video: 9-year-old boy sells rare baseball card for nearly $75,000
Ashby, who was 13-3 with a 3.12 ERA in 71 relief appearances during the season, has been untouchable in October. He's allowed five hits, walked three and has 19 strikeouts.
Miller had the longest streak of consecutive scoreless relief innings within one postseason with 16 in 2016 for Cleveland. Including the regular season, Ashby has thrown a career-best 22 2/3 straight scoreless innings.
Ashby had struggled in the postseason before this one. He allowed nine runs - eight earned - in 9 1/3 playoff innings over 10 appearances in 2021, 2024 and 2025.
Brewers relievers have allowed just eight earned runs over 60 2/3 postseason innings.

title: Trump says US will beat China in AI as technology emerges
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Artificial intelligence has emerged as the critical sticking point between the U.S. and China. President Donald Trump, who has named it “super intelligence,” insists the U.S. will beat China in the AI competition.
Trump said while campaigning for president that tariffs would form the crux of the bilateral relationship. The U.S. and China, the world’s two largest economies, have been engaged in a trade war during both of Trump’s terms.
Speaking Sept. 13 in Ireland, Trump said the U.S. is leading China in AI.
“We’re leading China in AI, we’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump said.
During a state visit to Beijing in May, Trump praised Chinese President Xi Jinping.
“And it’s to me an honor. We’ve had a fantastic relationship. We’ve gotten along. When they were difficulties, we worked it out,” Trump said.
Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September for a state visit. He touted what he called “the tremendous strides” he and Xi had already made on national security, trade and technology.
At the summit, the U.S. and China agreed to extend a trade truce until January. No agreement was reached on implementing safeguards for AI.
Trump and Xi are set to meet again in China next month.

title: International fugitive sentenced for one of the largest health care fraud schemes in U.S. history
text:
COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS/Gray News) - A man whom federal prosecutors called the architect of one of the largest health care fraud schemes in U.S. history was sentenced Monday.
Herbert Kimble was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with three years of court-ordered supervision. He was also ordered to pay more than $199 million in restitution to Medicare and forfeit more than $195 million in what prosecutors described as “ill-gotten gains.”
Kimble pleaded guilty in 2019 to conspiring to commit health care fraud, violate the anti-kickback statute, and defraud the United States in connection with a telemedicine and durable medical equipment scheme involving back, shoulder, wrist, and knee braces.
Prosecutors say Kimble ran offshore call centers that recruited elderly Medicare beneficiaries, paid kickbacks to telemedicine companies for signed prescriptions, then sold those orders to medical equipment companies that billed Medicare. Court filings put the intended loss at more than $400 million, with Kimble personally gaining more than $195 million.
Kimble cooperated with investigators in what became Operation Brace Yourself, but failed to appear for three court dates in fall 2024 and fled to the Philippines, where he remained a fugitive for nearly two years.
In June, the FBI named Kimble to its Most Wanted Fraudsters list. Days later, he was apprehended in the Philippines and returned to the United States. He later pleaded guilty to three counts of failure to appear as part of the 2026 National Health Care Fraud Takedown.
Bryan Stirling, U.S. attorney for the District of South Carolina, said Kimble’s sentence matches the seriousness of his crimes.
“Kimble orchestrated one of the largest international healthcare fraud schemes in our nation’s history,” Stirling said. “Today’s sentence underscores the seriousness of his crimes and reinforces the Department of Justice’s commitment to investigate and prosecute those who steal from American taxpayers.”
Kimble is not eligible for parole.
